subject: Post-call: snapshot of proprietary dependence + proposed next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@neuroscale.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: snapshot of proprietary dependence + proposed next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick notes from our side so we all have the same baseline and a suggested path forward.

TL;DR: Primary needs are lower per-token cost, consistent reranking outputs, and a path to validate model parity for your summarization and safety filters. We recommend a focused PoC to evaluate latency, cost, and quality with 2–3 open-model variants and a small inference-integrations checklist.

What you told us (pain points)
- Heavy spend on OpenAI for chat + embeddings; billing is unpredictable due to high-volume user flows.
- Latency spikes during peak hours (affects search & live chat flows).
- Summarization and moderation currently routed to Anthropic; outputs diverge from product expectations ~10–15% of the time.
- Concern about tokenizer/formatting parity for long documents and code snippets (important for your analytics ingestion).
- Need for deterministic reranking behavior (QA team requires repeatable outputs for A/B evaluation).

Current stack snapshot (as discussed)
- Chat/assistant: OpenAI GPT-4.1 via API (primary)
- Summarization: Anthropic Claude for long-form summaries
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, cached in Redis
- Orchestration: Kubernetes with a lightweight API gateway; logs forwarded to Splunk
- Volume: ~1.2B tokens/month (spike to 2B in marketing campaigns)

Success criteria for a replacement/PoC
- Cost: reduce inference TCO by ~35–50% at current volumes (target: 40%)
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 300ms for short responses, < 800ms for 2–3k token summaries
- Functional parity: match current summarization quality on your eval set (90%+ pass rate by your rubric)
- Ops: support streaming, function/tool calling (webhook triggers), and KV cache for chat context

Compatibility checklist (requirements you highlighted)
- Function-calling / tool invocation parity with your existing framework
- Streaming responses for low-latency UX
- Tokenizer compatibility for long docs (or clear migration mapping)
- Model quantization support (best-effort) for cost targets
- Audit logs + request tracing for compliance reviews

Model shortlist we propose for PoC (initial 2–3 demos)
- Llama-3-70B (int8) — strong chat baseline, good open-source ecosystem
- Mistral-Instruct-34B — efficient inference for instruction tasks
- Falcon-40B (opt) — good tradeoff for summarization and lower memory footprint
(we can swap in a 7B-class model for a latency-first PoC if you prefer)

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (60–90 min) with your infra + security engineering (Ben Carter from our solutions team) — schedule availability below.
2) Share a short PoC scope doc (attached) and a minimal dataset (your eval prompts + pass/fail rubric).
3) Security packet & SOC2 extracts request (we can pull the subset you need; see attached stub).
4) Quick commercial guardrail: preliminary cost estimate after we size the PoC (aim to provide within 3 business days).

Availability for TD: Mon/Tue next week 10–12 PDT or Wed 14–16 PDT — let me know what works.

Attachments: [Attachment: PoC-scope-v1.pdf (PDF, 92KB)], [Attachment: redwood-performance-profiles-link.txt (txt, 1KB)], [Attachment: SOC2-extract-request.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)]

Thanks — look forward to the next step.

—Karthik

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick response, and happy to take the deep-dive. Tue 2026-08-25 10:00–11:00 PDT works for me (I blocked it tentatively).

On the ballpark PoC cost: for a 2–3 week PoC to evaluate 2 model variants (one 70B int8 and one 40B opt), plus orchestration + integration work, typical ranges we see are $12k–$28k depending on throughput tested and dataset size. That includes engineering time (Redwood-managed PoC) and reserved inference capacity for the test window. We will refine after we size the eval prompts and desired concurrency.

Security notes: we can provide SOC2 extracts and a short data retention matrix. Logs: request-level traces are retained for 30 days in the default plan; we can extend retention or suppress storing raw prompts on request (we can also enable field-level redaction for PII). We'll bring our security lead if you want to walk the specifics on the TD.

- NeuroScale to share blind eval set (~250 prompts) + pass/fail rubric
